question: TypeORM vs Prisma with Nest — practical trade-offs?
shortAnswer: TypeORM: Active Record/Data Mapper, Nest module mature; Prisma: strong typing/DX, separate client lifecycle.
detailedAnswer: Either can work — migrations, transactions, and testing matter more than brand. Know N+1 risks in both.

question: Where should repositories live in Nest modules?
shortAnswer: As providers in the feature module (or dedicated persistence adapter module), injected into services.
detailedAnswer: Avoid controllers talking to ORM directly. Keep query details out of HTTP layer.

question: How do you handle transactions in Nest services?
shortAnswer: ORM transaction APIs / QueryRunner / Prisma $transaction; pass transactional client/unit-of-work through the use-case.
detailedAnswer: Don't open transactions in controllers. Watch request-scoped pitfalls. Keep transactions short.

question: N+1 queries in Nest resolvers/services — prevention?
shortAnswer: Eager/join appropriately, DataLoader for GraphQL, and explicit query planning — never lazy-load in loops blindly.
detailedAnswer: Log slow queries in staging. Review list endpoints for join strategies.

question: Migrations in production Nest apps — best practices?
shortAnswer: Expand/contract migrations, backward-compatible deploys, and never rely on synchronize in prod.
detailedAnswer: CI runs migrations with locks. Document rollback. Separate schema from data migrations.

question: Lead: multi-DB or CQRS read models with Nest?
shortAnswer: Separate modules/connections for write vs read, async projections, and clear consistency expectations.
detailedAnswer: Don't pretend every screen needs strong consistency. Own failure modes of projection lag.
